not_an_eligible_frame: All-positive domain criteria are necessary but not sufficient. Preferred-version, body, identity, sentinel and complete-frame gates remain.

rows.experiment_and_inference_rationale: The candidate responses are untrusted inputs to the protected judge. Perplexity/auxiliary known-answer decisions inspect that input; auxiliary detector output is not the protected judge response. English evaluated templates are explicit.
The same clean/injected data-block probe experiment supplies all criteria, including explicit pre-generation activations and English evaluated trigger constructions.

Embedding classifiers need only input prompt records, so timing follows from input-only computation. Mixed-language corpus contains an English component; held-out language composition and an English-only split are not claimed.
Original binary injection labels, English train/test curation and pre-target pipeline are all explicit in v1.
Clean/contaminated target-data decisions use a dedicated auxiliary detector secret check, not protected backend output. The actual detector instruction is evaluated in English.

Tool-description attack content is checked by a separate known-answer input detector with explicit injected/clean decisions. Its English secret-repetition instruction precedes any protected tool-use answer.
The dedicated detector labels data before forwarding to the distinct backend role; English evaluated detector construction is explicit.

Exact v1 separately checks clean/contaminated tool-input classification within the shared AgentDojo evaluation; this is distinct from environment-state agent-task checks. Original English attack constructions and pre-backend guard roles are supported in the same revision.
Original syntactic binary injection/opinion comparison runs on supplied English texts without protected consensus output. Identity/study overlap with thesis remains a separate hold.

Original synthetic-document experiment checks hidden instructions using extraction/OCR and phrase/optional detector flags. The detector's presence flag supplies the binary document decision and needs no protected LLM output. English injection constructions are explicitly evaluated.

The original contaminated-prompt residual classifier operates on final-input state, with any-segment binary aggregation. English instruction insertions are linked to long-context evaluation rather than inferred from corpus names.

Input detector baselines are separately evaluated from sanitization. Thresholded safe/unsafe input scores and auxiliary known-answer output precede the protected answer; held-out attack construction includes English overrides.

The original clean/injected email-prompt embedding drift experiment has explicit English filtering; encoded input pairs and flagging need no protected response. Availability of an aligned clean contrast is not a claim of deployability.
Original indirect-injection sequence classification explicitly precedes victim consumption and includes an English component of a multilingual benchmark.

Separate original input-text injection classifier comparisons qualify even though the main system monitors generated calls. Input classifiers need no protected output, and the actual cross-lingual set explicitly includes English.

Frozen-guard final-input features classify direct/indirect injection versus benign context before any guard verdict; no protected answer can be required. The source expressly limits evaluation to English. Offline input-only classification satisfies timing without demonstrating downstream deployment.

The studied benign/injection prompt guard is a binary natural-language input classifier, with windowing independent of a protected answer. The actual study uses English and Spanish, without implying all samples are English.
The original English rendered RAG-input benchmark has explicit benign/injection labels and a before-generation detector under external-content control.

Current publisher VOR methods expressly define binary input detection, pre-downstream/no-output timing and stated English single-turn evaluation. This establishes domain in those current bytes only; historical cutoff-version authentication remains a separate unresolved requirement.

All criteria are supported by the preferred ACL publication. Final-input/preset-reply features and explicit BIPIA pre-target screening do not require the protected answer; English original evaluation is distinct from translated extensions.
